sources.title: Writing and Rhetoric: Rhetoric and Contemporary Issues (21W.011, Fall 2015)
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
coursework: written assignments (3 essays, draft and revision)
sources.needIt: Teaches how to argue, read a speech or ad for what it is trying to do, and write so people act on it.
sources.notes: Undergraduate. OCW resource types listed: Presentation Assignments and Written Assignments; no lecture videos listed. A seminar course, so the units must be rebuilt as scenes rather than lectures.

sources.title: Writing and Rhetoric: Designing Meaning (21W.016, Fall 2016)
sources.by: Dr. Suzanne T. Lane, MIT Comparative Media Studies/Writing
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
coursework: essay assignments with draft and revision deadlines
sources.needIt: Shows how choices of words and layout change what a message means.
sources.notes: Seen in search results and its assignments page only; the course landing page was not opened, so licence is taken from the OCW Terms page that applies to all OCW. Reopen the course page to confirm before building.

sources.title: Introduction to Theory of Literature (ENGL 300)
sources.licenceSeen: Open Yale Courses Terms of Use page and the course page: 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 3.0 license'
sources.terms: Non-commercial only (Terms section 5). Third-party content is not covered unless a lecture's Credits section says so. Terms say nothing about AI or ingestion; check Yale's Office of General Counsel before any commercial use.
sources.needIt: Gives plain names to how a text means something, useful for reading news, contracts and arguments with a sharper eye.
sources.notes: Archive item holds 26 lecture audio files (mp3 and ogg), not video. Yale site lists 26 sessions. Required text is a commercial anthology, so reading lists are link only. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the Archive item is sound only (26 mp3); the filmed lectures play on the Open Yale course page. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the year is not on the page; read it from the title page before use.

sources.title: Modern Poetry (ENGL 310)
sources.licenceSeen: Open Yale Courses Terms of Use page and the course page: 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 3.0 license'
sources.terms: Non-commercial only (Terms section 5). Third-party content is not covered unless a lecture's Credits section says so. Terms say nothing about AI or ingestion; check Yale's Office of General Counsel before any commercial use.
coursework: two papers, midterm and final described
sources.needIt: A close reader's lesson in how a few words carry feeling, which helps with speeches, songs, toasts and eulogies.
sources.notes: Archive item holds 25 lecture audio files, not video. Readings come from a commercial anthology (link only); some poems are still in copyright, so quote nothing from them. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the Archive item is sound only (25 mp3); the filmed lectures play on the Open Yale course page.

sources.title: The Elements of Style
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Short rules for clear sentences that anyone can use in a text, a resume or a letter to a landlord.
sources.notes: Gutenberg lists the 1918 public-domain text, but the page does not show the year, so confirm the edition. Do NOT use the later Strunk and White editions (copyrighted). Some rules are style opinions, not law; flag them.

sources.title: How to Speak and Write Correctly
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Plain old-school guidance on common word mistakes and building a vocabulary.
sources.notes: Old English and some usage rules have changed (several 'errors' are now accepted). Flag the dated ones. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the year is not on the page; read it from the title page before use.

sources.title: The Art of Writing & Speaking the English Language
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Practice-based lessons on word choice and sentence building.
sources.notes: Ad-style language from the early 1900s; the rewrite should keep the exercises, drop the sales tone. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the year is not on the page; read it from the title page before use.

sources.title: On the Art of Writing
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Famous lectures on writing without padding, which helps anyone who has to write a report or a post.
sources.notes: Academic Edwardian voice; the rewrite should pick the practical bits (cut the jargon, be concrete). Audit 16 Nov 2026: lectures given at Cambridge in 1913 and 1914, published 1916.

sources.title: How to Write Letters (Formerly The Book of Letters)
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Teaches how to write a thank-you, a complaint, an invitation or a condolence note people will actually read.
sources.notes: Etiquette is dated (formal salutations, social customs). Keep the structure; update the manners and add email and text. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the year is not on the page; read it from the title page before use.

sources.title: Business English: A Practice Book
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Drills for the writing a job needs: short business letters, notes and reports.
sources.notes: Includes dated business forms (telegrams, carbon copies). Replace with current formats. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the year is not on the page; read it from the title page before use.

sources.title: Plain language guides (Digital.gov, adapted from PlainLanguage.gov)
sources.licenceSeen: Footer names the site as 'An official website of the U.S. General Services Administration'. No separate copyright statement on the page, so US federal authorship is the basis.
sources.needIt: The federal rules for writing so a tired person can understand a form, a notice or a bill, and the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
sources.notes: Four guides: principles, writing for understanding, design for understanding, testing for understanding. Header image is credited to a third party; do not reuse it. Confirm reuse wording on the site policy page before copying text word for word.
